skill.name: excalidraw-diagram-generator
skill.description: Generate Excalidraw diagrams from natural language descriptions, including flowcharts, mind maps, relationship diagrams, architecture diagrams, class diagrams, sequence diagrams, ER diagrams, and swimlane flows.
skill.summary: Create editable Excalidraw diagrams from plain-language requests.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown examples, Excalidraw source URLs, diagram text, and formatting backticks. The only confirmed issue is intended local filesystem write capability in helper scripts that modify user-selected diagram or library paths; no prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or malicious network behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts write to paths supplied on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict writes to expected .excalidraw files or library directories, resolve paths before writing, and warn users before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: The icon library splitter accepts any directory path and writes generated files inside it.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should run the splitter only on trusted local library directories and avoid running it on shared or sensitive paths.

content.value_statement: Turning ideas into clear diagrams can take time and require manual layout work. This skill converts natural language into editable Excalidraw files with structured layouts and opening instructions.
actual_capabilities: Creates Excalidraw JSON files that can be opened in Excalidraw.
Supports flowcharts, relationship diagrams, mind maps, architecture diagrams, data flow diagrams, swimlanes, class diagrams, sequence diagrams, and ER diagrams.
Uses bundled templates and schema references to format valid diagram elements.
Provides layout guidance for spacing, colors, labels, arrows, and element counts.
Includes optional Python helpers for adding arrows and icons to existing diagrams.
Can guide users through setting up Excalidraw icon libraries for cloud or infrastructure diagrams.
limitations: Generated diagrams are static Excalidraw files, not live interactive models.
Very large diagrams should be split into smaller diagrams for readability.
Icon-based diagrams require users to download and prepare compatible Excalidraw libraries.
The helper scripts modify local diagram files and should be run only on trusted paths.

use_cases.title: Document a Product Workflow
use_cases.description: Create a readable flowchart from a written process so teams can review steps and decisions.

use_cases.title: Sketch a System Architecture
use_cases.description: Generate an editable architecture diagram with components, connections, labels, and optional cloud icons.

use_cases.title: Explain a Data Model
use_cases.description: Turn entities, attributes, and relationships into an ER diagram that can be shared or edited.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Flowchart
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small process diagram.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excalidraw flowchart for this process: [describe the steps]. Use clear labels and save it as a .excalidraw file.

prompt_templates.title: Map Component Relationships
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for dependencies or service relationships.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a relationship diagram showing these components and connections: [list components and relationships]. Group related items and label every connection.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Cloud Architecture Diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excalidraw architecture diagram for this cloud system: [describe services, network boundaries, and data flow]. Use basic shapes unless an icon library is available.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Multi-View Diagram Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that should be split for clarity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a diagram plan for this complex system: [describe system]. Split it into a high-level overview and detailed sub-diagrams, then generate the first Excalidraw file.

output_examples.input: Create a flowchart for account registration with email verification.
output_examples.output: A .excalidraw flowchart with start, email entry, verification, password setup, success, and failure paths. The response includes a short summary and opening instructions.

output_examples.input: Diagram User, Post, and Comment relationships.
output_examples.output: An editable relationship diagram with three entities, labeled connections, consistent spacing, and a note explaining how to open it in Excalidraw.

output_examples.input: Create an AWS web app architecture diagram.
output_examples.output: A structured architecture diagram using zones, service labels, and arrows. If icon libraries are unavailable, it uses clear shapes and explains how to add icons later.

best_practices: Provide the main entities, steps, or actors before asking for a diagram.
Keep each diagram focused on one view or workflow for readability.
Review the generated Excalidraw file and adjust labels or spacing for presentation use.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for one diagram to cover every detail of a large system.
Do not run helper scripts on untrusted or sensitive file paths.
Do not assume optional icon libraries are available until their reference files are present.

faq.question: What file does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates an .excalidraw file that can be opened in Excalidraw or compatible editors.

faq.question: Can it create cloud architecture diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use basic shapes by default and can use prepared Excalidraw icon libraries when available.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: No for basic diagram generation. Users may visit Excalidraw or download optional libraries separately.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing diagram?
faq.answer: Yes. Bundled helper scripts can add arrows or icons to existing local .excalidraw files.

faq.question: What diagram types are supported?
faq.answer: It supports flowcharts, relationship diagrams, mind maps, architecture diagrams, data flow diagrams, swimlanes, class diagrams, sequence diagrams, and ER diagrams.

faq.question: What should I include in my prompt?
faq.answer: Include the diagram purpose, key elements, relationships, preferred layout, and any labels or constraints.
